criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Introduction clearly states coral-reef monitoring mission, rationale, single-spacecraft choice and users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university funding), with literature support. Minor referencing quality issues only.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Covers launch site/vehicle, SSO orbit and COEs, ground station, STK access/ground tracks, five-year duration and drag-sail EOL. Evidence is strong, but missing STK files, some technical slips (sunlight, RAAN, EOL manoeuvre) and unbuilt Vega E reduce confidence.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
The orbit is near-polar and retrograde
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved
A span of five years is a sound estimate of the useful lifespan

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion draws specific conclusions on launch, orbit and ground station and links them to mission benefit. It omits EOL/duration and some claims are generic, but appropriate.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.
A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering structure, executive summary and readable prose. However figures/tables are largely unnumbered, captions inconsistent, bibliography is URL-only, Wikipedia is used, and many table citations [49]-[74] are missing from the list.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite

technical_issues.issue: Uses Wikipedia [6] as a source, contrary to brief; many in-text citations [49]-[74] are absent from the reference list.
Figures and tables lack numbered captions/titles; Image 3 has no caption.
STK software files are not supplied; only screenshots and an access report are included.
States high altitude low resolution 'is also desirable' (contradiction); 'constant supply of sunlight' ignores eclipse periods.
RAAN 27.33° is described as indicating the launch facility; RAAN at epoch is not a direct launch-site indicator.
Calls EOL the only orbital manoeuvre, but the spacecraft has no thrusters and uses a passive drag sail.
Access table has a duplicate row/access numbering; minor data-quality issue.
Vega E is not yet built; schedule risk is acknowledged but the design depends on it.

overall: Comprehensive single-satellite GBR mission with STK access/ground-track evidence and all major design elements. Technical slips (sunlight, RAAN, EOL manoeuvre), missing STK files, unnumbered figures/tables, and weak referencing (Wikipedia, missing [49]-[74]) lower presentation.

feedback.summary: You present a comprehensive single-satellite GBR mission with strong STK evidence and all major design elements. Your introduction and conclusion are clear, and the mission design covers launch, orbit, ground control and EOL. To raise your presentation mark and strengthen the design, focus on numbered figure/table captions, complete referencing, supplying STK files, and resolving technical slips in orbit and EOL.
next_steps: Add numbered captions and titles to every figure and table (e.g., Image 1, Image 3, launch tables) and ensure each is referenced in the text; this directly addresses the Adequate presentation level.
Replace the Wikipedia source [6] with a credible reference, add all missing citations [49]–[74] to the bibliography, and check every in-text citation matches the reference list.

Supply the STK software files alongside your screenshots, and correct the technical slips: remove the 'high altitude low resolution is desirable' contradiction, clarify eclipse periods, explain RAAN correctly, and describe EOL as a passive drag-sail disposal rather than an orbital manoeuvre.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly defines the coral-reef monitoring mission, justifies a single spacecraft, and identifies users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university funding) with literature support. To secure a higher Accomplished mark, tighten referencing quality and ensure every claim is backed by a specific source; the content itself is already strong and well argued.
criteria.C2: Your mission design covers launch site/vehicle, SSO orbit and COEs, ground station, STK access/ground tracks, five-year duration and drag-sail EOL. Strong evidence, but missing STK files, technical slips (sunlight/eclipse, RAAN, EOL manoeuvre) and reliance on unbuilt Vega E reduce confidence. To reach the top of Accomplished, supply software files, resolve these inconsistencies, and add hand calculations or references that support each design choice.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion draws specific conclusions on launch, orbit and ground station and links them to mission benefit. To move from 7 to the top of the Accomplished band, include EOL and mission duration, and make each conclusion explicitly traceable to evidence in the main body rather than generic statements.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear engineering structure, executive summary and readable prose. However, figures/tables are largely unnumbered, captions are inconsistent, the bibliography is URL-only, Wikipedia is used, and citations [49]–[74] are missing from the list. To reach Accomplished, number and caption all figures/tables, use consistent formatting, and ensure every in-text citation matches a complete, credible reference list.
